newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines - April 4.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa's office has started drafting laws on the right of abode for foreign passport holders, which he could submit to the provisional legislature if the Sino-British Joint Liaison Group fails to reach an agreement.

-- SING TAO -- Property tycoon Li Ka-shing expressed confidence that the Hong Kong property market would not go down too much. He said he would not object to any action taken by the Real Estate Developers Association against the government regarding its recent measures to bring down property prices.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- A seminar was held in Beijing to commemorate the seventh anniversary of the establishment of the Basic Law, and Chinese leaders stressed that the Basic Law would guarantee that Hong Kong people would rule Hong Kong.

-- The chairman of China's National People's Congress, Qiao Shi, during a visit to Norway stressed the importance of the rule of law in China, which the third generation leadership were all agreed on.
-- ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Property experts estimated that property prices in Hong Kong would drop by three to 10 per cent in the second quarter.
-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Taipei said that direct shipping links across the Taiwan Strait, banned since 1949, could resume within just 10 days.
-- Hongkong Bank said that to finance yuan lending in Shanghai, it planned to rely on deposits rather than borrowing from China's interbank market, which was more expensive.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Encouraged by the success of Beijing Datang Power Generation's successful listing on the London Stock Exchange, Shanghai Electric Power said it too would seek a secondary listing on the London bourse.
-- The Hong Kong Securities and Futures Commission plans to relax key rules governing leveraged foreign exchange trading, giving greater flexibility to the industry while protecting investors.
